rule: Typed receivers (decision A, all statically typed languages and typed PHP/Groovy declarations): a receiver whose type is given by a declaration — local, parameter, field/property (including `$var->prop` / `obj.field` chains whose property has a declared type), catch parameter, for-loop variable, pattern binding — or by `= new T(...)` gives `T#m` (high if defined in the scan, else medium). | Rust constructors type their binding: `let x = T { .. }` and `let x = T::new(..)` / `T::default()` / `T::with_capacity(..)` give `x` type T; an in-scan associated function gives its declared return type (`-> Self`/`-> T`).
spec_gap: Does a Go short variable declaration type its binding for decision A? `a := &Dog{}` (composite literal) and `b := NewDog()` (in-scan function with declared return type *Dog) have no written type on the local. Decision A lists declarations and `= new T(...)`; the Rust ruling had to add `let x = T { .. }` and in-scan constructor/return types explicitly, implying the general rule does not cover them. Is a.Speak() / b.Speak() example.com/m.Dog#Speak (method, high) or `a.Speak` / `b.Speak` (method, low)? The same question applies to C# `var x = Make();` (C# `var x = new T()` is covered by `= new T(...)`).
notes: main -> example.com/m.NewDog (direct, high) is decidable; the two Speak calls are not.
